Title: When to pay for actions and actions modifiere

Messages.Author: Jesper
Messages.Body:
Hello all

If I make an actions which have some sort of cost, and then play an action
modifiere which also have some cost. Do I pay them at the same time, or one
after the other.

E.g. If I get one aggro damage from the action, and then one agro damage
from the action modifere do I the burn, or go to torpor loosing one blood?

Cheers

/Jesper

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Jesper wrote:
> Hello all
>
> If I make an actions which have some sort of cost, and then play an action
> modifiere which also have some cost. Do I pay them at the same time, or one
> after the other.

The cost of an action modifier is paid when it is played.
The cost of an action is paid when the action is successful.

> E.g. If I get one aggro damage from the action, and then one agro damage
> from the action modifere do I the burn, or go to torpor loosing one blood?

Actions and action modifiers cost blood or pool.
Damage is not the cost of a card (or action).

If the action or modifier inflicts damage, then that damage is inflicted at
the time indicated by card text. If two effects do damage at the same time,
you can order those effects.

On Tue, 7 Oct 2003 15:52:26 +0200, Jesper <26984...@mail1.stofanet.dk>
wrote:

> E.g. If I get one aggro damage from the action, and then one agro damage
> from the action modifere do I the burn, or go to torpor loosing one
> blood?

Lets say for example that a vampire bleeds with superior Force of Will. One
of prey's vampires attempts to block and then the acting vampire plays
Daring the Dawn and after that Conditioning to boost the bleed.

This is what happens to the acting vampire:
1st - play FoW and start the action
2nd - play DtD
3rd - play Conditioning and pay 1 blood
4th - reduce prey's pool by amount bled
5th - take 1 agg from FoW and 1 agg from DtD

If the acting vampire started with:
- 1 blood: action fizzles skipping step 4, vampire burns with 2 agg from
FoW and DtD
- 2 blood: action succeeds and after that vampire burns with 2 agg from FoW
and DtD
- 3 blood or more: action succeeds and after that vampire goes to torpor
and burns 1 blood from 2 agg from FoW and DtD

Messages.Author: Jeff Kuta
Messages.Body:
"Jesper" <26984...@mail1.stofanet.dk> wrote in message news:<3f82c49f$0$26165$ba62...@nntp05.dk.telia.net>...

> Hello all
>
> If I make an actions which have some sort of cost, and then play an action
> modifiere which also have some cost. Do I pay them at the same time, or one
> after the other.

You pay when the card is successful.

> E.g. If I get one aggro damage from the action, and then one aggro damage

> from the action modifere do I the burn, or go to torpor loosing one blood?

Taking aggravated damage occurs at resolution of the card, after costs
are paid. This may be declared in card text.

Say a vampire you control is forced to hunt going to 1 blood. Then you
decide to bleed at +2 bleed using Force of Will at superior. A vampire
attempts to block so you play Daring the Dawn at superior.

The action succeeds unblocked, so the vampire pays 1 blood going to
zero. The bled Meth takes 3. Then the acting vampire takes 2 points of
aggravated damage, burning in the process.

Here's another example:

A vampire you control has 1 blood and bleeds using Govern the
Unaligned. Depraved Thetmes attempts to block. You don't feel like
taking 2 aggravated damage so you desperately try to fish for stealth,
playing Conditioning, taking your vampire to zero blood. Luckily, you
draw into Lost in Crowds and stealth past Thetmes. Your action is
unblocked so now you pay costs for it to succeed. The vampire burned
his last blood for Conditioning, so the Govern fails (can't pay for
it) but at least your vampire survived for another turn.

Here's where I have a question now:
In the above scenario, was the action considered successful? It sounds
like the action was successful but fails due to non-payment. Suppose
Lucas Halton has 1 blood, a Fortitude skill card and the Ankara
Citadel. Lucas attempts to Clan Impersonate Assamites at +1 stealth.
Tariq Wakes then tries to stop him with +1 intercept since he's
already Draughted Anastazdi's Soul. Lucas further plays Alacrity for
+1 more stealth, paying his last blood in the process. Tariq lets the
action go unblocked.

Can Lucas play Freak Drive (for free) so he can try to hunt while
Tariq is still tapped? The action was successful (unblocked) but
failed due to lack of payment (no blood left).

Jeff

>failed due to lack of payment (no blood left).

I think that's where Freak Drive misses being able to be played. The
action wasn't successful (as it wasn't paid for). Freak Drive is only
playable after a sucessful action (at inferior) or after a block (at
superior). Neither of these is the case here, so freak drive cannot be
played at all.

Messages.Author: JH
Messages.Body:
On Wed, 8 Oct 2003 09:49:46 +0200, Jesper <26984...@mail1.stofanet.dk>
wrote:

> Dose that mean that you get one from the action modifere and then is
> wounded, then you get one aggro damage from the action and since your
> wounded is burned?

If a vampire is wounded and gets aggravated damage he must burn one blood
for every point of damage to avoid being burned. For example if a vampire
is going to torpor and in addition gets one aggravated damage he either
burns a blood or is burned.

As an answer to your question: yes if he had no blood, otherwise he can
burn blood equal to damage received to avoid being burned.

quote from Anarch rulebook, last paragraph on page 44:
"Aggravated damage done to a wuonded vampire can burn the
vampire outright. A wounded vampire is one that has taken
damage that he failed to heal or one that is in torpor or
on his way to torpor. For each point of aggravated damage
that is successfully inflicted on a wounded vampire, he must
burn a blood to prevent his destruction. If he doesn't have
enough blood, he is burned. Destruction by this method does
not constitute diablerie."

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Correct. If the action doesn't resolve (as in the case when the cost
cannot be paid), then Freak Drive cannot be played (since it can only
be played after resolution).

Normally this doesn't matter, since a fizzled action normally fizzles
because of lack of blood, and a lack of blood itself would preclude
Freak Drive.

But, for cases when an empty vampire could play Freak Drive, as above,
it still cannot be played if the action didn't get resolved (that is,
if the effects of the successful action weren't applied).
